lede: The DoW Contracting Professional certification in plain English: what it takes, in what order, how to sign up, and how the exam works.

phases.name: Guiding Principles
phases.plain: The basics that apply in every phase: who does what, what makes a contract, ethics, and writing things down.

phases.name: Pre-Award
phases.plain: Everything before offers arrive: the requirement, market research, the strategy and the solicitation. Six questions look at it from the seller's side.

phases.name: Award
phases.plain: From offers to a signed contract: pricing, negotiation, choosing the winner, and handling protests.

phases.name: Post-Award
phases.plain: After award: running the contract, making sure the work is right, subcontracts, changes, disputes and closeout.

requirements.title: 5 courses
requirements.body:
CON 1100 (or 1100V), CON 1200V, CON 1300V, CON 7300V and CON 1400V, from WarU (the Warfighting Acquisition University, formerly DAU) or an approved equivalent.

CON 7300V Price Analysis became required on 1 October 2026. Before CON 1300V you also finish five short online modules.

requirements.title: 1 exam
requirements.body:
CON 3990V, the Contracting Certification Exam: 150 multiple-choice questions in 3 hours, closed book, 70% to pass.

You take it at a Pearson test center (recommended) or online, and WarU pays for it.

requirements.title: 12 months
requirements.body:
of full-time experience doing a representative sample of contracting work.

Your component decides what counts. Documented equivalent experience from government or industry can be considered.

deadlines.label: The rule
deadlines.title: 36 months to get certified
deadlines.body:
From the day you enter a position that requires the Contracting Professional certification, you have a 3-year grace period (36 months) to earn it. Certification is a condition of employment for contracting-coded positions.
- The clock does not restart if you are promoted within contracting.
- It does restart if you leave a contracting-coded position and later come back.
- If you will miss it, your agency can request a waiver under DoDI 5000.66. Plan never to need one.

deadlines.label: Your unit
deadlines.title: Often 6 months for training and the exam
deadlines.body:
Many brigades and offices set a faster goal, such as finishing every course and the exam in your first 6 months, so you can start working toward a warrant sooner. That goal is local; ask your supervisor what yours is.

The certificate itself still needs 12 months of experience, so a 6-month goal really means: courses and exam done, experience on track.

roles.name: You
roles.does: Own your plan. Apply for courses early, attend full time, study every day, take the exam, and keep a record of the work you do.

roles.name: Your supervisor
roles.does: Approves your course and exam requests, protects your time during class, confirms your experience and supports your certification request.

roles.name: Acquisition Training Office (ATO)
roles.does: Your organization's training office. Approves training requests after your supervisor and answers registration questions.

roles.name: Army DACM Office (USAASC)
roles.does: The Army Director, Acquisition Career Management. Runs the Army acquisition workforce program, career records and certification, and answers help requests through the CAMP portal.

roles.name: WarU
roles.does: The Warfighting Acquisition University (the Defense Acquisition University until late 2025). Writes and teaches the courses and owns the certification exam.

roles.name: Pearson VUE
roles.does: The testing company that delivers CON 3990V at its test centers or online (OnVUE). WarU pays the fee.

roles.name: A mentor
roles.does: An experienced contract specialist or contracting officer who shows you how the work is really done. Ask your supervisor to assign one in your first week.

roles.name: 51C proponent and TAAS
roles.does: For Soldiers: the 51C proponent (in the Army DACM Office) and The Army Acquisition School in Huntsville, which runs the 9-week Army Acquisition Transition Course (AATC).

education: No degree is required for the certification itself. Hiring rules are separate: DoW 1102 positions require a bachelor's degree under 10 U.S.C. 1724 (the old rule requiring 24 business credit hours was removed in 2020). For 51C Soldiers, the Army sets the education standards for the MOS; ask your career manager or the 51C proponent.

register.intro: Army acquisition workforce members, Soldiers and civilians, apply for WarU instructor-led courses through **AITAS**, the Army's online training application, which feeds **ATRRS**, the Army's training records system. Some self-paced online WarU courses are taken directly in the WarU learning system instead; the course's page in the WarU iCatalog tells you which.

steps.t: Find the course and a class date
steps.d: Open the course in the WarU iCatalog and use Check Schedule. Write down the class number and dates. Pick a class that ends at least a week before the next course you need.
Make sure your name, organization and your supervisor's email address are right. A wrong supervisor email is the most common reason a request stalls.
In AITAS choose Student, then Apply for Training. Pick the course and class and submit. You need your CAC.
Your supervisor gets an email and approves in AITAS. Remind them politely; nothing moves until they do.
The Acquisition Training Office reviews and approves. Approved requests flow to ATRRS and then to WarU.

steps.t: Watch for the reservation and the welcome letter
steps.d: You get a reservation email. About 25 days before class, WarU sends a welcome letter with the links, any pre-work and a technical check. Do the pre-work: some courses grade it.
Virtual instructor-led (VILT) courses are full time. Your supervisor should put your workload on hold. Test your camera, microphone and the class software on the computer you will use.

register.verify: AITAS screens and approval routing differ by organization. Confirm these steps with your training NCO or Acquisition Training Office.
tips: Apply early. Seats fill fast. Ask your training office whether you may apply for the next course before you finish its prerequisite; usually the prerequisite only has to be done before that class starts.
While you wait for CON 1300V, finish its five online modules (FAC 069, FAC 082, FAC 085, CON 0074 and CON 0470) and keep the completion certificates. The instructor asks for them.
Already took an equivalent course at another agency or school? Ask about equivalency or fulfillment instead of taking it again.
Keep every completion certificate and your WarU transcript in one folder. You need them for certification and later for your warrant.
Reserve and National Guard Soldiers: some classes need orders or funding. Start with your unit training office.

facts.note: Multiple choice, drawn at random from a large bank
Includes the tutorial, breaks and your final review
Pass or fail. The FY26 average score was 74.8%
Completely closed book: no FAR, notes, phone or computer
Or online with OnVUE. Test centers pass about 4% more
WarU pays. A no-show still costs the Government a fee

exam.source: Sources: DoW Contracting Professional Certification Exam FAQs (as of 1 October 2026), CON 3990V User Experience Roadmap (11 May 2026), WarU iCatalog CON 3990V page and the Pearson VUE WarU page, checked 22 October 2026.

steps.d: You must be coded in the contracting functional area and have your supervisor's approval. Finish your courses first; CON 3910 (online exam prep) is strongly recommended before your first try.
Apply just like a course. AITAS will not let you register within 30 days of an earlier attempt or no-show, or for a fourth attempt inside 12 months.
Your supervisor and Acquisition Training Office approve. The approval flows through ATRRS to WarU, and WarU sends your name to Pearson.

steps.t: Look for the Authorization to Test email
steps.d: Pearson emails an Authorization to Test, usually within 24 hours of approval. Check your junk folder.

steps.t: Create a Pearson account and book a seat
steps.d: Use the WarU page at pearsonvue.com/us/en/waru.html. Choose a test center (recommended) or OnVUE. You have 90 days from authorization to take the exam.
No confirmation email means the booking did not finish; go back in and complete it. Pearson sends reminders 3 days and 1 day before.

Reschedule or cancel at least 48 hours ahead in your Pearson account. Rescheduling is free, but canceling without rescheduling uses one of your three attempts, and a no-show counts like a failed attempt. Inside 48 hours, your supervisor emails scheduling@waru.edu.

steps.t: Take it and read your score report
steps.d: You see the result when you finish. The report shows your percentage in four areas: Guiding Principles, Pre-Award, Award and Post-Award. A pass shows on your WarU transcript; WarU does not print a separate exam certificate.

testday: Bring a valid government-issued photo ID with a name that matches your Pearson profile exactly.
Arrive early; check-in takes a while. Your phone, smartwatch and notes go in a locker.
OnVUE (online) only: run the system check days before. Most government computers block the OnVUE software, so plan on a personal computer, a webcam, a quiet room and a clear desk.
Pace yourself at about 72 seconds a question. Flag the hard ones and come back.
Read every word. NOT, EXCEPT, FIRST and BEST decide many answers.
Answer every question. A blank is always wrong; a careful guess might be right.
retake: Wait at least 30 days, then apply again in AITAS. You get up to three attempts in 12 months.
After a first failed attempt, DoW requires **CON 3900V** (instructor-led exam prep) before your next try. CON 3910 is its prerequisite.
Use your score report. Spend most of your time on the area with the lowest percentage.

After a third failed attempt, review your exam feedback and both prep courses. Your agency must validate your remedial steps before you test again, and your DACM can approve more attempts case by case.

experience.intro:
The certification needs 12 months of full-time experience applying a representative sample of the contracting competencies. Your component decides what counts and your supervisor confirms it.

Use this list to track the kinds of work that build that experience. Ask your supervisor or mentor to let you do each one, then tick it. WarU also publishes an On-the-Job Training Tool for contract specialists that lists job tasks by competency; ask whether your office uses it.

items.text: Learn who the contracting officers in your office are and what their warrants allow
Finish your annual ethics training and know who your ethics counselor is
Build or reorganize a contract file so a stranger could follow the whole story
Review a purchase request for funding, a clear requirement and the right approvals
Do market research for a requirement and write it up
Help write or review a PWS, SOW or SOO and the IGCE
Check required sources and decide whether the buy is set aside for small business
Prepare and post a solicitation, answer vendor questions and issue an amendment
Evaluate quotes or proposals against the criteria in the solicitation
Determine and document a fair and reasonable price
Check responsibility: SAM registration, exclusions and the responsibility standards
Prepare an award and notify the unsuccessful offerors
Run or attend a post-award conference and work with a COR
Process a modification: an administrative change, funding or an option
Work an invoice or receiving report in PIEE and fix a payment problem
Write, or help write, a contractor performance assessment in CPARS

experience.note: This list is a study aid, not an official checklist. Your component sets the representative sample. Keep copies of your work (without sensitive or proprietary information) to show what you did.

after.cl:
Once certified, keep it current with **80 hours of continuous learning every 2 years** (DoDI 5000.66). DPCAP recommends that at least 40 of those hours be on contracting topics tied to your job.

WarU courses and credentials, webinars, conferences, college courses and some on-the-job assignments can count. Follow your component's process for recording them.
after.next:
Most new contracting professionals aim for a contracting officer warrant next. In the Army, warrants follow the Army Warranting Program Policy and usually include a Contracting Officer Review Board (CORB).

Board Ready, the warrant board study app from the same maintainer, picks up where this guide ends.

credentials.title: Advanced Contingency Contracting Credential

credentials.title: Operational Contracting Credential

after.reciprocity: The FAC-C (Professional) certification used by civilian agencies and the DoW Contracting Professional certification are treated as equal under a memorandum of understanding signed 16 October 2023, so your DACM can accept one for the other. If you came to DoW with only a legacy FAC-C, or none, ask your career manager what you still need. Civilian agencies require 100 continuous learning hours every 2 years; DoW requires 80.

faq.q: Do I have to finish in 6 months?
faq.a: The rule is 36 months for the whole certification. Many units set a faster local goal, often 6 months for the courses and the exam. Ask your supervisor what your goal is; My plan uses whatever goal you pick.

faq.q: Can I take the exam before I finish the courses?
faq.a: Eligibility for CON 3990V is being coded in contracting plus your supervisor's approval, and passing the exam never replaces a course. It is built to come after the courses, so finish them (and CON 3910) first. Your training office decides when you sit for it.

faq.q: Is the exam open book? Can I bring the FAR?
faq.a: No. It is completely closed book: no FAR, notes, books, phone or computer.

Weight your time like the exam: Guiding Principles 42 questions, Award 40, Post-Award 38, Pre-Award 30. Learn the titles of the 20 FAR parts the exam names, and read FAR Part 15 carefully; the exam FAQ says many questions come from it.

faq.q: Should I test online or at a test center?
faq.a: A test center, if you can. DoW data shows about a 4% higher pass rate at test centers, and most government computers block the OnVUE software anyway. If no center is within commuting distance, talk to your supervisor about travel before you schedule.
Wait at least 30 days and apply again; you get three attempts in 12 months. After a first failure DoW requires CON 3900V before the next try. Use your score report to focus on your weakest area.

faq.q: What is CON 7300V, and do I need it if I started before October 2026?
faq.a: CON 7300V Price Analysis became a required course for the DoW Contracting Professional certification on 1 October 2026, taken after CON 1300V. If you were already working on your certification, your component decides whether it applies to you, but DoW leadership expects you to take it. If you were certified before then, it is encouraged, not required.

Same school, new name. In late 2025 the Defense Acquisition University became the Warfighting Acquisition University (WarU) as part of DoW's acquisition transformation. Older links, certificates and people may still say DAU.

faq.q: What is the RFO, and does it change what I study?
faq.a: The Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) rewrote and renumbered much of the FAR. DoW adopted it through class deviations effective 1 February 2026, and the exam's answers now come from the RFO-updated FAR and DFARS. This guide uses RFO numbers; expect older materials to show old ones. See FAR & key numbers → Old → new numbers.

faq.q: Does the 51C course at TAAS count for any certification course?
faq.a: Verify locally. The 9-week Army Acquisition Transition Course (AATC) at The Army Acquisition School is the 51C MOS course. Check your WarU transcript and ask your training NCO or the 51C proponent which certification courses your records already show as complete.
Not for the certification. DoW 1102 hiring requires a bachelor's degree under 10 U.S.C. 1724. For 51C Soldiers, the Army sets MOS education standards.

faq.q: Does experience from before this job count?
faq.a: It might. Equivalent experience in government or industry can be considered if it is documented in detail. Your component decides.

faq.q: What if I miss the 36-month deadline?
faq.a: Certification is a condition of employment for contracting-coded positions. Without it, and without an approved waiver, you can face employment actions under your agency's procedures; Soldiers can face MOS-related actions. If you are falling behind, tell your supervisor early so a waiver can be requested in time.

faq.q: Who pays for the courses and the exam?
faq.a: WarU pays the exam fee. WarU courses for the acquisition workforce usually cost your unit nothing; travel for a classroom course is the usual exception. Ask your training office.

faq.q: How do I apply for the certification once I am done?
faq.a: Your component's process applies. In the Army, certification goes through the Army DACM Office's systems (the CAMP portal). Ask your supervisor or Acquisition Training Office to walk you through it, and have your transcript and exam result ready. Verify locally.
